summary: A history of armed civilian patrols on the US-Mexico border, from Texas Ranger violence and the 1977 Klan Border Watch to the Minuteman Project, Shawna Forde's 2009 Arivaca murders and 2019 vigilante detentions.

evidence.note: Texas Rangers act as first border force; 1910-1920 killings of Mexicans in the borderlands
1920s anti-Mexican sentiment and creation of the Border Patrol, its early brutality
Duke's October 1977 press stunt at the San Ysidro port launches the Klan Border Watch
Simcox biography begins: born 1961, Tombstone militia, Minuteman Project in 2005
Minutemen donation haul and mailing lists sold through conservative direct-mail firms
Forde's 2009 home invasion in Arivaca, Arizona kills a man and his nine-year-old daughter
April 2019 United Constitutional Patriots detain migrants in New Mexico; leader arrested

notes: Primary subject is a diffuse movement, so roles are empty. Transcript spells Forde as Ford and implies she was 41 in 2006; birth year left null rather than guess. Covered span starts with the 1910s Texas Rangers/Border Patrol segment (~8 min) as the stated origin of the story. US-AZ chosen as most central state, though TX, CA, WA and NM also appear.
